lane: Intensity: zone by new-fault density, then tile only what clears break-even
hypothesis: Faults that expert compilations add to a regional catalogue -- the population the competition scores -- are separable from background by an out-of-fold discriminant trained on off-catalogue map faults, and a sparse emission at that field's top ranks clears the exact marginal break-even bar.
mechanism: Presence-only discriminant (HistGradientBoostingClassifier) on 38 rank-transformed feature channels over the full 3730x3292 competition grid; positives = SGMC fault pixels > 300 m from the mapped catalogue (78,433 off-catalogue positives in the footprint, 61,664 beyond the 3 px collar); negatives = catalogue-free background; six spatially blocked folds; emission = top ranks of the pooled out-of-fold field, greedy 3.0 px minimum spacing, 30000 dots, catalogue pixels excluded from the candidate pool so all 30000 dots are off-catalogue.
named_non_fault_mimic: The SGMC off-catalogue population is ~6x more prevalent than the hidden 'new fault' population and mixes non-fault lineaments (unit contacts, thrust sheets, mining-district structures and compilation artefacts) with real faults; a classifier trained on it can reproduce compilation style rather than geology.

representation_aware.note: Overlap legs are reported per direction of support asymmetry and are not operative: at 3 px (300 m) two independent dot fields that both trace the same 60,988-point catalogue necessarily share neighbourhoods. The template's own shipped candidates fired the same legs (95 and 85 firings on full 695-raster scans) and were still shipped.

informative_forward_vs_smaller_or_equal_.reading: candidate duplicated into a peer that cannot cover it: THE operative forward leg

uninformative_forward_vs_bigger_peers.reading: a peer with far more support contains any candidate: non-operative (support asymmetry)

uninformative_reverse_vs_smaller_peers.reading: a sparse peer is necessarily covered by a denser candidate: non-operative

informative_reverse_vs_bigger_peers.reading: a bigger peer duplicated into the candidate: the operative reverse leg

representation_aware.note: Both informative directional legs are inside their limits (forward vs smaller/equal peers 0.2919, reverse vs bigger peers 0.4086 <= 0.70), so the only 3 px firings are the two documented uninformative directions. Operative registry leg = symmetric, scale-free statistics (worst |Spearman rho| 0.0636 <= 0.90; worst dot-set Jaccard 0.0209 <= 0.50; 0 byte-identical peers). The 3 px overlap legs are uninformative in both documented directions (IR-57-REPR-01): a continuous-surface peer laps every non-empty candidate forward, and a peer with far more support contains the candidate's dots whichever family the candidate belongs to. Every raw leg firing is preserved in 'literal_leg_firings' with its peer name, support and Jaccard.

uniqueness_h59j.verdict_registry_leg: no duplication identified: byte-unique, and every symmetric scale-free statistic is far below its limit (IR-57-REPR-01 representation-aware reading)

rules.forward: read only against peers whose expected 3 px disc coverage min(1, 29 * footprint_density) is <= 0.70
rules.reverse: read only against peers with >= 30 dots
rules.operative: byte identity + full-footprint Spearman + exact dot-set Jaccard + mutual 3 px coincidence (min of both directions, limit 0.70); every literal firing is listed

informative_forward.reading: candidate duplicated into a peer that cannot cover it

informative_reverse.reading: a peer with >= 30 dots duplicated into the candidate

mutual.reading: THE operative directional test: a near-copy must coincide in both directions

uninformative_forward_saturating_or_dens.reading: dense/regular peers whose discs already blanket the footprint: every non-empty candidate overlaps forward (IR-57-REPR-01)

uninformative_reverse_tiny_peers.reading: peers with < 30 dots: the fraction is 0 or 1 by luck

representation_aware.note: Operative registry leg = symmetric, scale-free statistics (worst |Spearman rho| 0.0636 <= 0.90; worst exact dot-set Jaccard 0.0209 <= 0.50; 0 byte-identical peers) PLUS the mutual 3 px coincidence (worst mutual 0.4086 <= 0.70, 0 firings). 80 literal one-sided leg firings are preserved in 'literal_leg_firings' with peer name, support and expected coverage; they lie in the two documented uninformative directions (IR-57-REPR-01).

instrument.evidence_class: PROXY-MEASUREMENT (off-catalogue SGMC proxy truth; not a competition score)

emission_design.selection_rule: criterion = T_proxy / (0.2*S_proxy + 0.8*G_calibrated), G_calibrated = 12700, truth = SGMC off-catalogue faults > 300 m from the catalogue; pre-declared. Reproduces the observed within-family live ladder (b2 > d2.8 > d1.5 > h19-5) which is the only regime where a local instrument has been shown to track the live board.

cross_family_rank_check.reading: within-family only; does not rank live scores across families

promotion_decision.verdict: negative: not cleared for a weekly submission slot
basis: No organizer-verified live score exists for this file and none is projected: the off-catalogue proxy criterion is calibrated within-family only.

Across artifact families the same proxy does not rank live scores: Spearman -0.057 (p 0.661) on 62 owner-reported anchors (the only significant term is credit-per-dot on the far collar, rho 0.252, p 0.048, and it is family-internal); the two direct off-catalogue emissions in the ladder scored 0.0512 and 0.0360 live against a 0.2778 incumbent.

The shipped raster measures criterion 0.3759 on the proxy truth (T 6350.0, S 33668.5, credit/dot 0.2117; evidence/h59j_emission_measurement.json), above the incumbent's 0.2952 -- but that ordering is within-family only and does not transfer live (the two cross-family artifacts above criterion 1.5 scored 0.036-0.051).

Emission design preferred spacing 3.0 px at 44090 dots (criterion 0.4606); the build used 30,000 dots because the owner live ladder is monotone down in budget, which makes the as-built arm the conservative choice, not the proxy-preferred one.

Registry leg is clean (695 rasters, 0 errors: 0 identical decoded predictions, worst |Spearman rho| 0.0636, worst exact dot-set Jaccard 0.0209; 80 literal 3 px firings are all in the two documented uninformative directions, IR-57-REPR-01), so the negative verdict is about the instrument, not about duplication.

Catalogue hide-and-recover holdout (HOLDOUT-DTI 0.082161, evaluator gems57-pooled-hide-v2, 11,321 withheld positives) remains below the published holdout best 0.135204, and the off-catalogue lane was built precisely because that instrument mis-ranks off-catalogue families (rho -0.544 with catalogue adjacency on live anchors).
promotion_decision.what_would_clear_it: an organizer-confirmed live score for an off-catalogue-family emission at or above the incumbent 0.2778, or a lane whose cross-family proxy ranks live scores (|rho| with p < 0.05 in the right direction) and whose top arm beats the incumbent's proxy criterion
promotion_decision.owner_action: selector step; this project does not pick or consume submission slots
